name: LongFact Concepts
description: LongFact is a benchmark for evaluating long-form factuality in large language models. It comprises 2,280 fact-seeking prompts spanning 38 topics, designed to test a model's ability to generate accurate, long-form responses. The benchmark uses SAFE (Search-Augmented Factuality Evaluator) to evaluate factual accuracy.
evaluation_method: SAFE (Search-Augmented Factuality Evaluator) — fraction of supported atomic facts
general_score_metric: F1 score (precision and recall of supported atomic facts)
typical_sota_score: ~70-85% F1 (frontier models; factuality degrades for obscure topics)
reputation: Published at COLM 2024; introduces SAFE automated factuality evaluation framework; widely adopted for measuring long-form factuality; from Google DeepMind
notes: Published at COLM 2024 by Google DeepMind. LongFact-Concepts covers facts about concepts (broader than LongFact-Objects which covers specific entities). Contains 2,280 prompts across 38 diverse topics. SAFE evaluates factuality by decomposing responses into atomic claims and checking each against Google Search. Two variants: LongFact-Concepts (broader) and LongFact-Objects (entity-specific).
